title: Aspect
about: Almost every Greek verb has two stems: the imperfective (*γράφ-*) for actions seen as ongoing or repeated, and the perfective (*γράψ-*) for one complete action. After *θα*, *να*, *ας*, in the imperative and in the past you must choose. A one-off action takes the perfective; a habit or a background action takes the imperfective. The perfect tenses (*έχω*, *είχα*) always use the perfective form *γράψει*.

items.en: Tomorrow I'll write you an email.

errs.why: One action in the future, done once: perfective *θα γράψω*. *Θα γράφω* means "I'll be writing / I'll write regularly".

items.en: I'll have a coffee and then I'm off.

errs.why: One coffee, once: *θα πιω* (perfective of *πίνω*).

items.en: I want to read for half an hour every day.

errs.why: A habit (*κάθε μέρα*) takes the imperfective: *να διαβάζω*. For one time, *θέλω να διαβάσω αυτό το βιβλίο*.

items.en: Can you help me now?

errs.why: A single request for now: perfective *να με βοηθήσεις*.

items.en: Close the door, please.

errs.why: For one action the imperative is perfective: *κλείσε*, *άνοιξε*, *πες μου*. *Κλείνε* means "keep closing it / close it every time".

parts: Κάθε πρωί πίνω έναν καφέ και διαβάζω τις ειδήσεις.
items.en: Every morning I drink a coffee and read the news.
items.why: Nothing to fix: the present tense is always imperfective, and the habit fits it.

items.en: When I was a child I used to go to the village every summer.

errs.why: Repeated past habits take the imperfective past: *πήγαινα*. The aorist *πήγα* is for one trip.

items.en: Last year I went to Crete for a week.

errs.why: One finished trip: aorist *πήγα*.

items.en: While I was writing the email, the phone rang.

errs.why: The background action that was going on uses the imperfective (*έγραφα*); the event that interrupts it uses the aorist (*χτύπησε*).

items.en: I have read all her books.

errs.why: The perfect is *έχω* + the perfective form in *-ει*: *έχω διαβάσει*, *έχω γράψει*. There is no *έχω διαβάζει*.

items.en: I haven't seen the new film yet.

errs.why: *βλέπω* has the perfective stem *δ-*: *θα δω*, *να δω*, *έχω δει*.

items.en: As soon as I finish, I'll call you.

errs.why: After *μόλις*, *όταν*, *αφού* about the future, use the perfective subjunctive: *μόλις τελειώσω*.

parts: Μην ανησυχείς, θα σου τηλεφωνώ κάθε βράδυ.
items.en: Don't worry, I'll call you every evening.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *κάθε βράδυ* is a repeated future action, so the imperfective *θα τηλεφωνώ* is right.

parts: Κάθε φορά που τον συναντούσα, μου
items.en: Every time I met him he told me the same story.

errs.why: *κάθε φορά που* describes a repeated past situation, so both verbs are imperfective: *συναντούσα… έλεγε*.

items.en: By eight I had finished the work.

errs.why: The pluperfect is *είχα* + perfective form: *είχα τελειώσει*.

items.en: In a year I'll have finished my studies.

errs.why: A completed point in the future: *θα τελειώσω* or, stressing completion by then, *θα έχω τελειώσει*.

parts: Τον περιμέναμε μία ώρα και τελικά
items.en: We waited for him for an hour and in the end he came by taxi.

errs.why: The arrival is one completed event: aorist *ήρθε*.

parts: Όσο έβρεχε, καθόμασταν μέσα και παίζαμε τάβλι.
items.en: While it was raining we sat inside playing backgammon.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *όσο* "while" frames ongoing background actions, all imperfective.

items.en: Since she moved, she rarely visits us.

errs.why: *σπάνια* describes a habit, so the present (imperfective) *επισκέπτεται*. *Επισκεφτεί* is a perfective subjunctive and cannot stand alone.

items.en: If you had come earlier, you would have met her.

errs.why: Unreal past condition: *αν* + pluperfect, *θα* + pluperfect: *αν είχες έρθει, θα την είχες γνωρίσει*.

items.en: The committee is expected to examine the matter next Tuesday.

errs.why: One completed future act on a set date: perfective *να εξετάσει*.

items.en: The writer wrote the novel in three months.

errs.why: *Σε τρεις μήνες* measures how long it took to complete, so the aorist: *έγραψε*. With *για τρεις μήνες* "for three months" the imperfective *έγραφε* is natural.

parts: Τα τελευταία χρόνια διαβάζω πολύ λιγότερο απ' ό,τι
items.en: In recent years I read much less than I used to read as a student.

errs.why: A habit over a stretch of the past ("used to read") takes the imperfective: *διάβαζα*.

items.en: As soon as the news arrived, the market reacted.

errs.why: *μόλις* with a single past event takes the aorist: *μόλις έφτασε*.

parts: Θα σας ενημερώνουμε τακτικά για την πορεία της έρευνας.
items.en: We will keep you regularly informed about the progress of the investigation.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *τακτικά* signals repetition, so the imperfective future *θα ενημερώνουμε* is right.
